A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PROSE research work. All 28 pages of v2 and 29 pages of v3, including figures, equations, tables, and appendices, support comparison. Reordered appendix material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original molecular sampling experiments, baseline comparisons, architecture ablations, dataset-scaling tests, and temperature-transfer results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark tables and supplementary evaluations.

M1.justification: The architecture, training objective, and sampling families are retained. However, Appendix E.1 changes generation from the inverse flow to the forward flow and alters the centroid correction, inconsistently with retained definitions. The PDFs do not resolve whether these represent intended procedural changes or transcription errors.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ManyPeptidesMD coverage, peptide benchmarks, and temperature-transfer scenario. The nine-residue YQNPDGSQA and ten-residue Chignolin evaluations already appear in v2; their relocation in v3 adds no coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain ECNF, ECNF++, TarFlow, TimeWarp, BioEmu, UniSim, molecular dynamics, and the same sampling algorithms. The relocated JSD and sequence-extrapolation tables retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: Figure 9 changes the reported dataset-scaling evaluation from 10 test octopeptide sequences to 30 octopeptide sequences. This is a limited reported sample-size revision; the unchanged plotted values do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The architecture and lookahead ablations, dataset-scaling curves, temperature tests, extrapolation cases, and qualitative analyses are retained. The added compute-budget caveat interprets existing evidence rather than introducing another analysis.

E5.justification: Seed information and statistical reporting practices are unchanged, including the unique seeds used for distributed ECNF++ sampling. No repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Matched tables retain their numerical performance entries, and all twelve figure graphics are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains PROSE's octopeptide E-W2 of 10.038 and TICA-W2 of 0.988. The JSD and extrapolation tables are reordered without changing their findings.

T1.justification: Equation 37 changes the centroid quadratic term from positive to negative after expanding the brackets, so it is not an equivalent rewrite. Section 2.1 and Appendix A.1 also make the Jacobian summation explicit over blocks and coordinates. The existing AIS/SMC derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about transferable sampling, efficient likelihood evaluation, competitive SNIS/self-improvement, and released resources. Reporting 4.3 ms of training simulation summarizes the existing dataset rather than expanding the contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix F.3 newly qualifies the dataset-scaling findings as potentially compute-limited: the subsampled dataset supports over 800,000 nonrepeating training batches, exceeding the 500,000-step budget. This adds a substantive caution to the retained scaling interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies training-trajectory subsampling to 10 ps per frame and normalization constants of 0.35 for eight-residue data or 0.28 for four-residue data. These refine previously general preprocessing descriptions without establishing changed training runs. Resource-access disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 replaces the description of Tan et al. (2025) as reducing SNIS variance with an account of extending Boltzmann generators to more general Monte Carlo algorithms. Equation 6 also gains explicit attribution to Klein and Noe (2024). The bibliography is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 edits introduction/background prose, adds an appendix contents page and architecture subsections, and reorders appendix sections. These are targeted organizational changes. It also introduces the malformed 'bsectionEffective sample per second' heading and the typo 'Temperature Plops'.

P2.justification: Appendix tables and Figure 6 move with the reordered sections, while the JSD and extrapolation tables exchange positions and numbers. JSD column labels gain 'k', and Figures 5 and 9 receive caption corrections. The figure graphics themselves are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves appendix navigation, preprocessing disclosure, Jacobian clarity, and interpretation of dataset scaling. However, Appendix E.1 introduces a forward/inverse-flow inconsistency, and Equation 37 reverses a sign incompatibly with the stated density correction. These technical regressions compete with the documentation gains; the unchanged empirical evidence does not resolve the intended prescription, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
